result:
Divisors d < M/100 correspond under d ↦ M/d to divisors greater than 100. So M is imbalanced exactly when the number a of divisors ≤ 100 satisfies a < 0.01·τ(M), i.e. τ(M) > 100a. (Solution 1 wrongly claims this is impossible; the argument fails because "divisors > 100" is not the same set as "divisors < 50".)

The divisors of 2000 that are ≤ 100 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 16, 20, 25, 40, 50, 80, 100. That is 13 divisors, including 100 itself, so a ≥ 13 and τ(M) > 1300.

If M has exactly 2^4·5^3 as its 2- and 5-part and every other prime factor exceeds 100, then a = 13 and τ(M) = 20·P for an integer P. The smallest multiple of 20 above 1300 is 1320. It is achieved by M = 2000·p^65 with p > 100 prime, which gives τ = 20·66 = 1320.

Any other form of M adds more small divisors. For example, 2^5 adds 32, so a ≥ 14 and τ ≥ 1401. So the minimum is 1320.

Solution 2 reaches 1320. Its count of 12 small divisors is slightly off, since it uses "<100" in places and so omits 100, but the final answer is correct.

Solution 3 counts only 12 divisors (it lists 13 but says 12), so its threshold 1200 and its answer 1220 are wrong.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: ACCEPT
VERDICT 3: REJECT
